notes: SECOND, corrected pass. Naming-collision census for this book (flagged explicitly on every affected entry): three separate "Azariah"s (son of Oded 15:1; the chief priest who opposes Uzziah 26:17-20; son of Johanan among Ahaz's-era Ephraimite leaders 28:12) plus Ahaziah of Judah's own KJV variant name "Azariah" at 22:6 - four uses of the name total. Three separate "Zechariah"s (son of Jehoiada, manager tier; the unnamed-elsewhere seer who instructed Uzziah, 26:5; and Hezekiah's maternal grandfather, 29:1, citation-only). "Jehoram"/"Joram" used interchangeably for TWO different contemporaries in 21:5-22:7 - Jehoram king of Judah (this book's own manager tier) and Jehoram/Joram king of Israel, Ahab's son (22:5 uses both spellings for him in adjacent clauses). "Jehoahaz" used for two different kings of Judah: Ahaziah (21:17, alternate name) and Josiah's son who reigned 3 months (36:1-4). "Joash"/"Jehoash" used for both Joash king of Judah (manager tier) and Joash king of Israel, who defeats Amaziah in 25:17-24 - flagged even though not in the original issue list, since it is the same type of collision this book is riddled with. "Manasseh" is used as a tribal/territorial name (31:1, 34:6) distinct from King Manasseh. Athaliah's own parentage is an intra-book crux: 21:6 calls her "the daughter of Ahab" while 22:2 calls her "the daughter of Omri" (Ahab's father) - hedged, not resolved. Michaiah (Abijah's mother, 13:2) is a near-homograph of Micaiah the prophet (18:4ff) - different people, flagged. Jehoiachin's age at accession (36:9, "eight years old") conflicts with 2 Kings 24:8 ("eighteen"); Zedekiah is called Jehoiachin's "brother" in 36:10 though he was actually Josiah's son (Jehoiakim's brother, Jehoiachin's uncle) per 2 Kings 24:17/Jeremiah - both hedged as well-known textual cruxes, not silently resolved. Direction of the Huram/Solomon city exchange corrected to match 2 Chronicles 8:1-2's own wording (Huram restored cities TO Solomon), which differs from the account in 1 Kings 9:10-13 - Chronicles' own text is followed, not assumed to match Kings. The craftsman sent by King Huram is named exactly as KJV gives it, "Huram his father" (4:16), not the NIV-style "Huram-abi" - and flagged as sharing the name "Huram" with the king who sent him. Chronicles' own sparser wording is followed where it omits detail 2 Kings supplies (e.g., Sennacherib's death: Chronicles does not name his sons or his god, unlike 2 Kings 19:37, so none are asserted here). No dedicated law/ritual tiers were used for this book - 2 Chronicles is royal narrative history throughout, unlike the Pentateuch books; every tier here is a person.

characters.name: Solomon

genealogy.note: Full genealogy is 1 Chronicles' domain; 2 Chronicles opens with Solomon already established as king.

verses.note: Asks God for wisdom at Gibeon rather than riches.
Builds and dedicates the Temple; fire from heaven consumes the sacrifice (7:1).
Visited by the Queen of Sheba.
Reigns 40 years, dies, succeeded by Rehoboam.

funFacts: Wisdom request and Temple-building are both original to this narrative arc, unlike some later kings whose stories are compressed.

characters.name: Huram, King of Tyre

genealogy.note: Foreign king; no Judean lineage given.

verses.note: Correspondence with Solomon; supplies cedar/fir/algum timber and sends the craftsman "Huram his father."

CORRECTED direction: "the cities which Huram had restored to Solomon, Solomon built them" - Huram gives/restores cities TO Solomon, not the reverse (contrast 1 Kings 9:10-13, a different account not assumed to carry over unchanged).
His servants, with Solomon's, bring gold and algum trees from Ophir; joint navy to Tarshish.

funFacts: Shares the name "Huram" with the craftsman he personally sends to Solomon (2 Chr 2:13) - flagged as an intra-book name collision, king and craftsman both called Huram.

characters.name: Huram his father (the craftsman)
characters.perkNote: Sent personally by King Huram as a skilled gift to Solomon's temple project; boosts Huram king of Tyre's tier.

genealogy.mother: a woman of the daughters of Dan (2 Chr 2:14)
genealogy.note: KJV literally names him "Huram his father" (2 Chr 4:16) - NOT the NIV-style "Huram-abi." Flagged: shares the name Huram with the king who sent him, a distinct person.

verses.note: Sent by King Huram, "endued with understanding," skilled in gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, timber, and engraving.
Makes the pots, shovels, fleshhooks, and all the bronze Temple furnishings; called "Huram his father" throughout.

characters.name: The Queen of Sheba
characters.perkNote: Her admiring testimony to Solomon's wisdom and wealth boosts Solomon's tier.

genealogy.note: Unnamed beyond her title; no genealogy given.

verses.note: Tests Solomon with hard questions, is overwhelmed by his wisdom and the Temple, blesses the LORD.
Exchanges gifts with Solomon; gives gold, spices, and precious stones.

characters.name: Rehoboam

genealogy.note: No further naming notes beyond his mother, Naamah, and his large family listed in ch.11.

verses.note: Rejects the elders' counsel, answers the people harshly; ten tribes revolt under Jeroboam.
Fortifies Judah's cities; large family.
Forsakes the law of the LORD; Shishak of Egypt invades; Shemaiah's word; Rehoboam humbles himself.

funFacts: The kingdom split (ch.10) and Shishak's invasion (ch.12) both happen in his single reign.

characters.name: Shemaiah the Prophet
characters.perkNote: Prevents a civil war and later softens judgment on Rehoboam - boosts Rehoboam's tier.

genealogy.note: Also cited (12:15) as a historiographic source for Rehoboam's acts, in addition to his active scene role.

verses.note: Stops Rehoboam from attacking the ten tribes: "this thing is done of me."
Tells Rehoboam and the princes, fleeing before Shishak, that God has given them up because they forsook Him; they humble themselves.

characters.name: Shishak, King of Egypt
characters.perkNote: His invasion strips the Temple's treasures - reduces Rehoboam's tier cost.

genealogy.note: Foreign king; no genealogy given in this book.

verses.note: Invades Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year with a vast Egyptian/Libyan/Sukkiim/Ethiopian army; takes the Temple and palace treasures, including Solomon's gold shields.

characters.name: Jeroboam

children: a son named Abijah, per 1 Kings 14 - not detailed in 2 Chronicles' own text
genealogy.note: 2 Chr 10:2 notes he had earlier fled to Egypt from Solomon; fuller family/tribal background belongs to 1 Kings, not restated here.

verses.note: Returns from Egypt, becomes leader of the ten northern tribes after Rehoboam's harsh answer.
Wars against Abijah of Judah at Zemaraim; loses despite an ambush; struck by the LORD, dies (13:20).

funFacts: CORRECTED: Jeroboam is not a one-scene character confined to the ch.13 battle - he is the central antagonist of the entire kingdom-split narrative in ch.10 as well.

characters.name: Abijah

genealogy.mother: Michaiah/Maachah, daughter of Uriel of Gibeah (13:2) - also called "Maachah the daughter of Absalom" at 11:20-21, a well-known textual crux not resolved here (Uriel may have married a daughter/descendant of Absalom).
genealogy.note: Reigned only 3 years (13:2).

verses.note: Defeats Jeroboam at Zemaraim after a covenant-themed speech; 500,000 Israelite soldiers slain (a large round number, per the text).

funFacts: His mother's name "Michaiah" (13:2) is a near-homograph of the unrelated prophet Micaiah (18:4ff) - different people, flagged to avoid confusion.

genealogy.note: No further naming notes beyond the collision flags on his own submanagers below.

verses.note: Removes idols; defeats Zerah the Ethiopian's massive army at Mareshah.
Reforms the kingdom after Azariah son of Oded's prophecy.
Allies with Syria against Israel instead of trusting God; rebuked by Hanani, imprisons him; diseased feet in old age; dies.

characters.name: Zerah the Ethiopian
characters.perkNote: An invading force whose defeat is credited to Asa's faith - reduces Asa's tier costs.

genealogy.note: Identified in the text only as "Zerah the Ethiopian"; no further genealogy given.

verses.note: Invades with "a thousand thousand" (a large round number) and 300 chariots; routed by Asa's army with the LORD's help.

characters.name: Azariah the son of Oded
characters.perkNote: His prophetic encouragement sparks Asa's reform - boosts Asa's tier output.

genealogy.note: NOTE: distinct from the later prophet Oded (28:9), whose father is not given - do not conflate the two Odeds.

verses.note: Meets Asa after the Zerah victory; "the LORD is with you, while ye be with him"; prompts covenant renewal.

characters.name: Hanani the Seer
characters.perkNote: Rebukes Asa's misplaced trust in Syria - fits the "opposes the major" pattern.

children: Jehu the seer/prophet (probable, hedged - see jehu_son_of_hanani)
genealogy.note: Probably the father of Jehu the seer who later rebukes Jehoshaphat (19:2, 20:34); the shared unusual name and "seer" title make this likely but the text does not state it with certainty.

verses.note: Rebukes Asa for relying on Syria's king rather than the LORD; Asa imprisons him in a rage.

characters.name: Jehoshaphat

genealogy.note: No further naming notes beyond the collisions flagged on his submanagers below.

verses.note: Strengthens Judah, sends teachers of the law throughout the land.
Allies with Ahab of Israel by marriage; joins him at Ramoth-gilead against Micaiah's warning.
Rebuked by Jehu the seer; institutes judicial reforms.
Delivered from a Moabite/Ammonite coalition after Jahaziel's word; the battle is the LORD's.
Allies with Ahaziah king of Israel on a doomed Tarshish shipbuilding venture; condemned by Eliezer; the ships are broken.

funFacts: His many alliances with the northern kingdom (Ahab, then Ahaziah of Israel) are each rebuked by a different prophet in turn - Micaiah, Jehu, and Eliezer.

characters.name: Ahab, King of Israel
characters.perkNote: His ill-advised alliance nearly costs Jehoshaphat his life - reduces Jehoshaphat's tier cost.

genealogy.father: Omri (well known from Kings, not detailed in 2 Chronicles' own text)
children: a daughter, Athaliah, given in marriage to Jehoram of Judah (21:6) - see athaliah for a parentage crux
genealogy.note: Appears in 2 Chronicles only within the ch.18 Ramoth-gilead episode.

verses.note: Persuades Jehoshaphat to join him against Ramoth-gilead.
Disguises himself in battle but is struck by a random arrow and dies, as Micaiah foretold.

characters.name: Micaiah the son of Imlah
characters.perkNote: Vindicates Jehoshaphat's instinct to seek a true prophet - boosts Jehoshaphat's tier.

genealogy.note: Not to be confused with Michaiah, Abijah's mother (13:2) - different name-spelling, different person, different gender.

verses.note: Summoned at Jehoshaphat's request; alone among the prophets predicts Ahab's death; struck by Zedekiah son of Chenaanah; imprisoned on bread and water.

characters.name: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah
characters.perkNote: A false prophet whose confident wrong counsel is exposed - his presence marks a costly near-miss for Jehoshaphat.

genealogy.note: NOTE: shares the name "Zedekiah" with the final king of Judah (ch.36) - a different, unrelated person, flagged.

verses.note: Makes iron horns, prophesies Ahab's victory over Syria.
Strikes Micaiah on the cheek after being contradicted.

characters.name: Jahaziel
characters.perkNote: His word of assurance secures the Moab/Ammon victory - boosts Jehoshaphat's tier.

genealogy.father: Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph (20:14)
genealogy.note: His father is yet another "Zechariah" - a fourth use of the name in this book, though purely genealogical with no independent scene of his own.

verses.note: "The battle is not yours, but God's"; instructs Judah not to fight but to stand still and see the LORD's salvation.

characters.name: Jehu the son of Hanani
characters.perkNote: Rebukes Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahab - reduces Jehoshaphat's tier cost.

genealogy.note: The text calls him "Jehu the son of Hanani" but does not explicitly confirm identity with Asa's rebuker beyond the shared name and title; hedged, not asserted as certain.

verses.note: Meets Jehoshaphat on his return from Ramoth-gilead: "Shouldest thou help the ungodly...wrath is upon thee."
Cited as the source recording "the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat."

characters.name: Eliezer the son of Dodavah
characters.perkNote: Condemns the Tarshish venture, whose failure marks a real setback - reduces Jehoshaphat's tier cost.

genealogy.note: No further genealogy given beyond his father's name and hometown, Mareshah.

verses.note: "Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the LORD hath broken thy works"; the Tarshish ships are wrecked and never sail.

funFacts: Newly added - the whole 20:35-37 Ahaziah-of-Israel/Tarshish episode was previously missing from this index.

characters.name: Ahaziah, King of Israel
characters.perkNote: An incidental ally whose partnership dooms the Tarshish fleet - reduces Jehoshaphat's tier cost.

genealogy.note: CRITICAL: a DIFFERENT person from Ahaziah, King of Judah (ch.22, its own manager tier) - this is Ahab's son, king of the northern kingdom, one generation earlier. Do not conflate.

verses.note: Joins Jehoshaphat to "make ships to go to Tarshish"; the ships are broken and never make the voyage, per Eliezer's condemnation of the alliance.

funFacts: Newly added figure, distinct from Judah's Ahaziah.

characters.name: Jehoram (Joram), King of Judah

children: several older sons, killed by Arabian/Philistine raiders (21:17)
genealogy.note: No further naming notes beyond the major collision described in funFacts below.

verses.note: Murders his brothers upon taking the throne.
Walks in the ways of the kings of Israel because of his marriage to Athaliah; Edom and Libnah revolt.
Receives a written condemnation from Elijah.
Raided by Philistines/Arabians, who kill his sons and wives except Ahaziah; dies of an incurable bowel disease; "departed without being desired," not buried in the sepulchres of the kings.

funFacts: FLAGGED: shares the name "Jehoram"/"Joram" with his own contemporary and brother-in-law, Jehoram (Joram) king of Israel, Ahab's son - see jehoram_king_of_israel. The two are easily confused since both names are used for both men across 21:5-22:7.

characters.name: Elijah the Prophet
characters.perkNote: His written condemnation marks Jehoram's reign as judged - reduces Jehoram's tier cost.

genealogy.note: His famous ministry from 1 Kings is not retold here; only this one letter appears in 2 Chronicles.

verses.note: Sends a letter pronouncing a plague on Jehoram's people, wives, and goods, and a bowel disease on Jehoram himself.

characters.name: Ahaziah, King of Judah

genealogy.note: Also called "Jehoahaz" (21:17, as the youngest/sole surviving son) and, per a KJV textual variant, "Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah" (22:6). Reigned only one year (22:2).

verses.note: Made king after his brothers are slain; walks in the counsel of Ahab's house through his mother Athaliah.
Joins Jehoram of Israel against Hazael of Syria at Ramoth-gilead; visits the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel; his death there is "of God."
Found hiding in Samaria and killed by Jehu (of Nimshi, a different, unrelated Jehu from 2 Kings, not detailed in this book).

funFacts: Two naming notes on this single king: (1) also called "Jehoahaz" at 21:17; (2) the KJV literally reads "Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah" at 22:6, a well-documented KJV-specific variant referring to this same Ahaziah.
CRITICAL: distinct from Ahaziah, King of Israel (ch.20:35-37, Ahab's son, a full generation earlier) - do not conflate the two Ahaziahs.

characters.name: Jehoram (Joram), King of Israel
characters.perkNote: His war-wound draws Ahaziah to his death - reduces Ahaziah's tier cost.

genealogy.note: CRITICAL COLLISION: called BOTH "Jehoram" and "Joram" within the same short span (22:5 uses "Jehoram the son of Ahab" then "Joram" for the same man in the same verse) - and this is the identical name already used for Jehoram king of Judah (a separate manager tier, Ahaziah's own father). The two Jehorams are contemporaries and brothers-in-law (Jehoram of Judah married Ahab's daughter Athaliah, Jehoram of Israel's sister).

verses.note: Wounded by the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead; called "Jehoram" and "Joram" for the same person within these two verses.
Visited by Ahaziah of Judah at Jezreel, precipitating Ahaziah's own death.

characters.name: Joash (Jehoash), King of Israel
characters.perkNote: Defeats and humiliates Amaziah - reduces Amaziah's tier cost.

genealogy.father: Jehoahaz of Israel (well known from Kings, not detailed in 2 Chronicles' own text)
genealogy.note: CRITICAL: shares the name "Joash" with Joash, King of Judah (his own manager tier, ch.24) - a completely different person, one generation earlier. Flagged even though not in the original issue list, since it is the same type of collision this book is riddled with.

verses.note: Answers Amaziah's challenge to battle with the fable of the thistle and the cedar.
Defeats and captures Amaziah at Bethshemesh, breaks down part of Jerusalem's wall, plunders the Temple and takes hostages.

genealogy.note: CRUX, hedged: 21:6 calls her "the daughter of Ahab" but 22:2 calls her "the daughter of Omri," Ahab's father - both used of her within this same book. Possibly "daughter" is used loosely for granddaughter/descendant in one of the two verses; not resolved here.

verses.note: Her counsel leads her son Ahaziah into wickedness.
On Ahaziah's death, destroys all the royal seed of Judah and reigns 6 years, except that Jehoshabeath hides the infant Joash.
Discovers the coronation of Joash, cries "Treason," is put to death at the horse gate entrance.

characters.name: Jehoiada the Priest

genealogy.note: Dies at age 130 (24:15) - an unusually long life, noted plainly by the text.

verses.note: His wife Jehoshabeath hides the infant Joash in the house of God.
Orchestrates the covenant and coronation of the seven-year-old Joash, arranges Athaliah's death, destroys the house of Baal.
Guides Joash's early, faithful reign; arranges two wives for him.
Dies at 130, is buried among the kings "because he had done good in Israel."

funFacts: Effectively co-regent/regent for the boy-king Joash - promoted to his own tier here rather than treated as a mere submanager, since his actions are the load-bearing hinge of the entire Athaliah-to-Joash transition.

characters.name: Jehoshabeath
characters.perkNote: Her rescue of the infant Joash preserves the Davidic line - boosts Jehoiada's tier.

genealogy.note: Daughter of King Jehoram and sister of Ahaziah of Judah (22:11) - royal blood married to the high priest.

verses.note: Steals the infant Joash from among the king's sons about to be slain and hides him in the Temple for six years.

genealogy.note: CRITICAL: shares the name "Joash"/"Jehoash" with Joash, King of Israel (see joash_king_of_israel) - a different person who later defeats Amaziah.

verses.note: Crowned at 7; under Jehoiada's guidance, repairs the Temple through a collected offering.
After Jehoiada's death, turns to idolatry at the princes' urging.
Has Zechariah, Jehoiada's own son, stoned in the Temple court.
Judah invaded by Syria; Joash is wounded, then killed in his bed by his own servants; not buried in the sepulchres of the kings.

characters.name: Hazael, King of Syria
characters.perkNote: His invasion drains Joash's treasury and marks the reign's decline - reduces Joash's tier cost.

genealogy.note: Foreign king; no genealogy given in this book.

verses.note: Invades Judah and Jerusalem; destroys the princes; Judah's small army defeats a much larger Syrian force "because they had forsaken the LORD."

characters.name: Zabad the son of Shimeath
characters.perkNote: One of Joash's assassins - marks the tragic end of his tier.

genealogy.note: CORRECTED per 2 Chronicles' own wording (24:26): named "Zabad," not "Jozachar" - the spelling used in the parallel account at 2 Kings 12:21. This book's own text is followed rather than assuming the Kings spelling carries over.

verses.note: Conspires against and kills Joash in his bed.

characters.name: Jehozabad the son of Shimrith
characters.perkNote: Co-conspirator in Joash's assassination.

genealogy.note: No further genealogy given beyond his mother's name and origin.

verses.note: Conspires with Zabad against and kills Joash.

characters.name: Zechariah, son of Jehoiada

genealogy.mother: Jehoshabeath (probable, as Jehoiada's wife, though not stated explicitly as his mother)
genealogy.note: A well-known crux: Matthew 23:35 refers to "Zacharias son of Barachias," slain "between the temple and the altar" - widely debated whether this is the same Zechariah, since the patronym given there (Barachias) does not match Jehoiada. Hedged, not asserted as the same identification.

verses.note: Rebukes Joash and the princes for forsaking the LORD; stoned by the king's command in the court of the LORD's house; dying words, "The LORD look upon it, and require it."

funFacts: Promoted to his own tier rather than a mere submanager: his murder is the direct narrative pivot that brings judgment on Joash's reign (24:24-25) - a load-bearing scene, not an incidental one.

genealogy.note: No further naming notes beyond the collision flagged on joash_king_of_israel below.

verses.note: Executes his father's murderers but spares their children per the law of Moses.
Hires, then dismisses, Israelite mercenaries at an unnamed man of God's word; defeats Edom, brings back their gods.
Rebuked by an unnamed prophet for worshipping Edom's gods; provokes and is defeated by Joash of Israel.
Conspired against, flees to Lachish, is killed there.

genealogy.note: Also called "Azariah" in the parallel account (2 Kings 15) - a cross-book variant, briefly noted, not detailed further since 2 Chronicles itself consistently uses "Uzziah."

verses.note: Prospers greatly "as long as he sought the LORD"; builds, farms, and strengthens the army.
Grows proud, unlawfully burns incense in the Temple, is struck with leprosy and confronted by Azariah the priest and 80 priests.
Lives out his days a leper, buried in a field belonging to the kings, "for they said, He is a leper."

characters.name: Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God
characters.perkNote: His instruction underwrites Uzziah's early prosperity - boosts Uzziah's tier.

genealogy.note: A THIRD distinct "Zechariah" in this book, alongside Zechariah son of Jehoiada (ch.24, his own manager tier) and Jahaziel's father Zechariah (20:14) - all different, unrelated people.

verses.note: "He sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper."

characters.name: Azariah the Priest
characters.perkNote: Confronts Uzziah's overreach into the priesthood - reduces Uzziah's tier cost.

genealogy.note: One of THREE distinct "Azariah"s in this book - see the notes field at the top level. Not to be confused with Azariah the son of Oded (ch.15) or Azariah the son of Johanan (ch.28), nor with Ahaziah of Judah's KJV variant name "Azariah" (22:6).

verses.note: Goes in with 80 priests to withstand Uzziah's unlawful incense offering; leprosy breaks out on Uzziah's forehead as they confront him.

genealogy.note: No further naming notes; a brief, uneventful chapter by this book's standards.

verses.note: Builds the high gate of the Temple, fortifies cities, defeats the Ammonites and exacts tribute; "became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD."

characters.name: Ahaz

genealogy.note: No further naming notes beyond the Azariah collision flagged on azariah_son_of_johanan below.

verses.note: Walks in the ways of Israel's kings, makes molten images, burns his children in the fire.
Defeated by Syria and by Pekah, king of Israel, who kills 120,000 in one day and takes captives.
Appeals to Assyria for help, which distresses rather than strengthens him; shuts up the Temple doors.

funFacts: The Israelite army's captive-release, prompted by Oded and four named Ephraimite leaders, happens within his reign (28:9-15) even though the confrontation itself takes place in Samaria, not before Ahaz directly.

characters.name: Oded the Prophet
characters.perkNote: Secures the captives' release, an act incidental to (not directly involving) Ahaz himself - reduces Ahaz's tier cost.

genealogy.note: Distinct from the earlier Azariah the son of Oded (15:1) - if related, the text does not say so; not assumed to be his father.

verses.note: Meets Israel's army returning to Samaria with Judahite captives; "deliver again the captives... for the fierce wrath of the LORD is upon you."

characters.name: Azariah the son of Johanan
characters.perkNote: One of four Ephraimite leaders who stand with Oded to secure the captives' release.

genealogy.note: A SECOND "Azariah" in this book alongside Azariah the son of Oded (15:1) and Azariah the priest (26:17) - three distinct people of this name, plus Ahaziah of Judah's KJV variant name "Azariah" (22:6), a fourth use.

verses.note: One of the heads of the children of Ephraim who "stood up against them that came from the war" and insisted the captives be released.

funFacts: Newly added along with the other three leaders below - previously missing from this index.

characters.name: Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth
characters.perkNote: One of the four Ephraimite leaders securing the captives' release.

genealogy.note: No further genealogy given beyond his father's name.

verses.note: Named among the four Ephraimite leaders opposing bringing the captives into Samaria.

characters.name: Jehizkiah the son of Shallum
characters.perkNote: One of the four Ephraimite leaders securing the captives' release.

genealogy.note: No further genealogy given beyond his father's name; not assumed related to other Shallums in scripture without textual support.

verses.note: Named among the four Ephraimite leaders opposing bringing the captives into Samaria.

characters.name: Amasa the son of Hadlai
characters.perkNote: One of the four Ephraimite leaders securing the captives' release.

genealogy.note: Not to be confused with the unrelated Amasa of 2 Samuel/1 Chronicles, David's general - a different person, not detailed in this book.

verses.note: Named among the four Ephraimite leaders opposing bringing the captives into Samaria.

genealogy.note: His mother's father is yet another "Zechariah" - a purely genealogical mention, no independent scene.

verses.note: Cleanses and reopens the Temple in his first year.
Celebrates a great Passover, inviting even the remnant of the northern tribes.
Organizes priestly/Levitical courses and tithes; destroys high places "in Ephraim also and Manasseh" - a territorial, not personal, use of "Manasseh" (see manasseh's entry).
Withstands Sennacherib's invasion; prepares Jerusalem's defenses and the water conduit.
Falls sick and recovers; pride and the Babylonian envoys; dies, buried "in the chiefest of the sepulchres."

characters.name: Isaiah the Prophet
characters.perkNote: Prays with Hezekiah against Sennacherib - boosts Hezekiah's tier.

genealogy.father: Amoz (well known from Isaiah 1:1, not restated in 2 Chronicles' own text)
genealogy.note: Full genealogy and independent ministry belong to the book of Isaiah; only these two mentions appear in 2 Chronicles.

verses.note: Prays together with Hezekiah against Sennacherib's threat.
Cited as recording "the rest of the acts of Hezekiah" in his vision.

genealogy.note: 2 Chronicles does NOT name his sons or the god in whose house he is slain (contrast 2 Kings 19:37, which names Adrammelech, Sharezer, and Nisroch) - not asserted here since this book's own text omits them.

verses.note: Invades Judah, besieges the fenced cities; Hezekiah prepares Jerusalem's defenses and rallies the people.
Sends servants to blaspheme the LORD and urge surrender.
The LORD sends an angel who destroys his army; he returns home in shame.
Slain by "them that came forth of his own bowels" (his own sons) in the house of his god - names not given in this account.

characters.name: Manasseh

genealogy.note: As king, not to be confused with the tribal/territorial name "Manasseh" used elsewhere in this book - see funFacts.

verses.note: Extreme idolatry: rebuilds high places, sets up altars to Baal, makes his children pass through fire, uses divination.
Carried in fetters to Babylon by Assyrian captains; humbles himself greatly, prays, and is restored to his kingdom - material largely omitted from the parallel account in 2 Kings.
Fortifies cities, removes the idols, repairs the altar of the LORD after his repentance.

funFacts: FLAGGED: "Manasseh" also names a tribal territory in this book, distinct from King Manasseh - "in Ephraim also and Manasseh" (31:1, under Hezekiah's reforms) and "the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon" (34:6, under Josiah's reforms), both referring to the tribal land, not this king.

genealogy.note: No further naming notes; his conspirators are unnamed in this book's text.

verses.note: Reigns 2 years, does evil like his father before Manasseh's repentance but "humbled not himself... as Manasseh his father had humbled himself"; killed by his own servants in his house.
The people of the land kill the conspirators and make Josiah king in his place.

children: Zedekiah (called Jehoiachin's "brother" at 36:10, though genealogically Josiah's son and thus Jehoiakim's brother/Jehoiachin's uncle - see zedekiah's entry for this crux)
genealogy.note: 2 Chronicles does not name Josiah's mother (contrast 2 Kings 22:1, "Jedidah") - not imported here since this book's own text omits it.

verses.note: Begins seeking God at 16, purges idolatry from Judah and "in the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon" (a territorial use of "Manasseh," distinct from the king) at 20.
Repairs the Temple; Hilkiah finds the book of the law; Shaphan reads it to the king.
Sends a delegation, including Hilkiah and Shaphan, to inquire of the LORD; Huldah the prophetess delivers her oracle.
Celebrates the greatest Passover "since the days of Samuel the prophet."
Disguises himself to fight Necho of Egypt at Megiddo despite Necho's warning; is mortally wounded and dies.
Jeremiah laments for him; the lamentation becomes an ordinance in Israel.

characters.name: Hilkiah the Priest
characters.perkNote: His discovery of the book of the law triggers Josiah's whole reform - boosts Josiah's tier.

genealogy.note: Possible, unconfirmed identity with the Hilkiah named as Jeremiah's father (Jeremiah 1:1) - a traditional association some hold, but the text of 2 Chronicles does not itself link the two; hedged, not asserted.

verses.note: Finds "the book of the law of the LORD given by Moses" in the Temple.
Sent, with others, to inquire of the LORD concerning the book.

characters.name: Shaphan the Scribe
characters.perkNote: Reads the newly found law to Josiah, triggering the king's response - boosts Josiah's tier.

children: Ahikam (34:20, part of the same delegation to Huldah - see genealogyLists)
genealogy.note: No further genealogy given beyond his son Ahikam, who is part of the same delegation sent to Huldah.

verses.note: Receives the book from Hilkiah and reads it before the king.
Sent with Hilkiah and others to inquire of the LORD.

characters.name: Huldah the Prophetess
characters.perkNote: Confirms the book's authority and Josiah's own favorable end - boosts Josiah's tier.

spouses: Shallum the son of Tikvah, keeper of the wardrobe (34:22)
genealogy.note: NOTE: her husband's father "Shallum" is a common name; not assumed related to Jehizkiah the son of Shallum (28:12), a different Shallum.

verses.note: Delivers the LORD's oracle: judgment is coming on Judah, but not in Josiah's own days, because his heart was tender.

funFacts: The only prophetess given a full recorded oracle in 2 Chronicles.

characters.name: Jeremiah the Prophet
characters.perkNote: Laments Josiah and later confronts Zedekiah - boosts Josiah's tier.

genealogy.note: His extensive independent ministry belongs to the book of Jeremiah; only these three mentions appear in 2 Chronicles.

verses.note: Laments for Josiah; his lamentations are still referenced "in the lamentations" as an ongoing ordinance.
Zedekiah does not humble himself before Jeremiah, "speaking from the mouth of the LORD."
His word about the land's sabbaths/seventy years is fulfilled by Cyrus's decree.

characters.name: Pharaoh Necho, King of Egypt

genealogy.note: Foreign king; no genealogy given in this book.

verses.note: Warns Josiah not to fight him at Megiddo ("I come not against thee this day... forbear thee from meddling with God"); Josiah is mortally wounded in the ensuing battle.
Deposes Jehoahaz after 3 months, fines Judah 100 talents of silver and a talent of gold, makes Eliakim king in his place and renames him Jehoiakim; carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

funFacts: Spans two different kings' reigns (kills Josiah, then deposes Jehoahaz) - promoted to his own tier rather than a submanager under either single king, since his role is genuinely load-bearing across both transitions.

genealogy.note: CRITICAL: shares the name "Jehoahaz" with the alternate name of Ahaziah, King of Judah (21:17) - a completely different king, three generations earlier. Flag both entries.

verses.note: Made king by the people of the land; reigns only 3 months before Necho deposes him, fines Judah, and carries him captive to Egypt.

genealogy.note: Originally named Eliakim; renamed "Jehoiakim" by Pharaoh Necho (36:4). Brother of Jehoahaz.

verses.note: Reigns 11 years, does evil; Nebuchadnezzar binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon and takes vessels from the Temple.

characters.name: Nebuchadnezzar, King of Babylon

genealogy.note: Foreign king; no genealogy given in this book.

verses.note: Comes against Jehoiakim, binds him, takes Temple vessels to Babylon.
Sends for and brings Jehoiachin to Babylon with more Temple vessels; makes Zedekiah king in his place.
Sends the Chaldean army to destroy Jerusalem and the Temple after Zedekiah's rebellion; carries the survivors captive to Babylon.

funFacts: Central antagonist across three successive kings' reigns (Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, Zedekiah) - promoted to his own tier rather than repeated as a submanager under each.

genealogy.note: 36:9 gives his age as "eight years old" - conflicting with 2 Kings 24:8's "eighteen years old," a well-known textual crux between the two accounts, hedged rather than resolved here.

verses.note: Reigns only 3 months and 10 days; carried to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar along with Temple vessels; Zedekiah made king "his brother" in his place.

characters.name: Zedekiah

genealogy.father: Josiah (per genealogical reckoning elsewhere in scripture, making him Jehoiakim's brother and Jehoiachin's uncle)
genealogy.note: CRUX: 2 Chr 36:10 itself calls him Jehoiachin's "brother" when made king - but he is elsewhere understood (2 Kings 24:17) as Jehoiachin's uncle (Josiah's son, Jehoiakim's brother). Hedged, not silently resolved, since this is the wording of Chronicles' own text.

verses.note: Made king by Nebuchadnezzar at 21; rebels against him and stiffens his neck against the LORD.
Along with the priests and people, pollutes the Temple and mocks the LORD's messengers, until there is "no remedy."
Jerusalem and the Temple are destroyed by the Chaldeans; the land lies desolate to fulfil the word by Jeremiah's mouth.

funFacts: The last king of Judah in this book's narrative.

characters.name: Cyrus, King of Persia

genealogy.note: Foreign king; no genealogy given in this book.

verses.note: His spirit is stirred by the LORD to fulfil Jeremiah's word; issues a proclamation permitting the exiles to return and rebuild the Temple at Jerusalem - the book's closing verses.

funFacts: The book ends mid-proclamation, on an upward, hopeful note despite the preceding destruction.

genealogyLists.hezekiah_temple_cleansing_levites_29_12_: CORRECTED 14-name list of Levites who cleanse the Temple: Mahath, Joel, Kish, Azariah (son of Jehalelel), Joah, Eden, Shimri, Jeiel, Zechariah, Mattaniah, Jehiel, Shimei, Shemaiah, Uzziel. 'Jehalelel' is NOT a 15th name - he is the father of Azariah (one of the 14), per 29:12's own wording ('Azariah the son of Jehalelel'). Bulk names with no individually differentiated action beyond the collective cleansing; not given separate character entries.
genealogyLists.jehoram_slain_brothers_21_2_4: Jehoram of Judah's six brothers, killed by him on taking the throne (21:2-4): Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah, all sons of Jehoshaphat. NOTE: two of the six brothers are BOTH named 'Azariah' within the single verse 21:2 - a striking intra-verse naming collision. Undifferentiated group beyond being named and slain; not given separate character entries per the 'undifferentiated named group' rule.
genealogyLists.josiah_huldah_delegation_34_20: The full delegation Josiah sends to inquire of the LORD via Huldah (34:20): Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah a servant of the king's. Only Hilkiah and Shaphan the scribe are given full character entries (they have independently differentiated actions elsewhere in the narrative - finding and reading the book); Ahikam, Abdon, and Asaiah appear only as part of this single collective errand with no individually differentiated action, so are noted here rather than given separate entries.
genealogyLists.prophetic_source_citations: Several named prophets are cited in this book only as historiographic sources for the formulaic 'the rest of the acts of [king] are written in the book/vision of [prophet]' - not as active scene participants: Iddo the seer (9:29, re Solomon; 12:15, re Rehoboam's genealogies; 13:22, re Abijah) and Nathan the prophet (9:29, re Solomon). These are citation-only (pure transmission/bibliographic), with no personally-embodied action in 2 Chronicles' own text, so are not given individual character entries - contrast Shemaiah and Jehu the son of Hanani, who are also cited as sources but additionally appear in real, personally-embodied scenes and so do receive full entries.
genealogyLists.manasseh_territorial_name_note: 'Manasseh' is used as a tribal/territorial name at 31:1 ('in Ephraim also and Manasseh,' under Hezekiah's reforms) and 34:6 ('the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon,' under Josiah's reforms) - both referring to the tribal territory, not King Manasseh (his own manager tier, ch.33). A real intra-book collision between a place-name and a tracked person.
genealogyLists.pekah_king_of_israel_note: Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, is named at 28:6 as slaying 120,000 men of Judah in one day during Ahaz's reign. A real, named figure, but his role in this book is a single summary statistic with no scene or dialogue (contrast Oded, who has an extended speech and named companions); noted here rather than given a separate character entry.
